question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase.

In the absence of government rule, riots have broken out all over the country and everything is in a state of complete chaos.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Anarchy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "in the absence of government rule" with "riots" and "complete chaos" describes a state of lawlessness and disorder. The word that captures this is "anarchy" — a situation of disorder due to the absence of authority or government. (अराजकता)

◦ Correct: In the absence of government rule, everything descends into anarchy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Oligarchy" = rule by a small privileged group.

• Option 3 "Dictatorship" = rule by a single all-powerful person.

• Option 4 "Monarchy" = rule by a king or queen.

NOTE

• Related terms: anarchy (no government/order), democracy (rule by the people), aristocracy (rule by the nobility), theocracy (rule by religious authority), plutocracy (rule by the wealthy).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The detail given by the instructor was the ______ one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. most updated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" before the blank and the singular noun "one" signal the superlative degree, so "the most updated one" is correct. "Updated" also works as a past-participle adjective describing "detail". (सबसे नवीनतम)

◦ Correct: The detail given by the instructor was the most updated one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more updation" — "updation" is non-standard and "more" (comparative) does not fit "the ... one".

• Option 3 "updating" and Option 4 "updates" are grammatically wrong here (a form of "one" needs an adjective).

NOTE

• With a long adjective, the superlative is formed with "the most" (the most updated / the most modern), while the comparative uses "more ... than".

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

You can do your work well within the stipulated time and be more productive if you learn to keep video games at the length of your arm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. at arm’s length.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "at arm’s length" means to keep someone/something at a distance; to avoid becoming too involved. It fits the sense of keeping video games away/at a distance. (दूरी बनाए रखना)

◦ Correct: ... if you learn to keep video games at arm’s length.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 distort the fixed idiom ("at arm of his length", "at arm’s weight", "at arm of your length") and are not standard English.

NOTE

• Note the possessive form "arm’s" (singular possessive). Similar distance idioms: "keep at bay", "give a wide berth", "steer clear of".

question:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.

Looking up, she realised she had swum __________ than she’d thought.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. farther.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Farther" is the comparative of "far" used for physical/measurable distance. As "swum" refers to an actual distance covered in water, "farther than" is correct. (अधिक दूर)

◦ Correct: ... she had swum farther than she’d thought.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "furthest" and 3 "farthest" are superlatives and cannot be used with "than".

• Option 4 "further" is generally used for abstract/figurative extent (e.g., "further information", "further discussion"), so "farther" is the better fit for literal distance.

NOTE

• Farther/farthest → physical distance; further/furthest → additional/abstract degree. With "than" a comparative (farther/further) is required, not a superlative.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

The recommendations of the committee / regarding changes in the eligibility criteria / was not accept.
option_2: regarding changes in the eligibility criteria
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. was not accept.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "recommendations" is plural, so the verb must be plural — "were", not "was". Also, after "were not", the past participle "accepted" is needed (passive voice), not the base verb "accept". So the segment should be "were not accepted".

◦ Correct: The recommendations of the committee regarding changes in the eligibility criteria were not accepted.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The recommendations of the committee" and "regarding changes in the eligibility criteria" are grammatically correct.

• The error is one of both subject–verb agreement and passive-voice form.

NOTE

• Passive voice = be-verb + past participle (V3): "were accepted", "was rejected". Ensure the be-verb agrees with the real subject (recommendations → were).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He sings good / among all the / contestants in / the singing competition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He sings good.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sings" is a verb and must be modified by an adverb, not the adjective "good". The correct adverb is "well". So it should be "He sings well".

◦ Correct: He sings well among all the contestants in the singing competition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "among all the", "contestants in" and "the singing competition" are all correct.

• "Good" describes a noun (a good singer); "well" describes how an action is done (sings well).

NOTE

• Common adjective/adverb confusions: good/well, bad/badly, quick/quickly. Verbs of action take adverbs (runs fast, works hard, sings well).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. paralel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Paralel" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "parallel" (having two l’s), meaning side by side and always the same distance apart; comparable. (समानांतर)

◦ Spelling key: PAR + AL + LEL — note the double "l".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "humorous" (funny), "achieve" (to accomplish) and "familiar" (well known) are all correctly spelt.

• Remember "achieve" follows the rule "i before e except after c".

NOTE

• Frequently misspelt: parallel, necessary, occurrence, embarrass, millennium — watch the double letters carefully.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Consciencious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Consciencious" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "conscientious", meaning careful, thorough and taking one’s duties seriously. (कर्तव्यनिष्ठ)

◦ Spelling key: CON + SCIEN + TIOUS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Unanimous" (in complete agreement), "Millennium" (a period of 1000 years) and "Inconvenience" (trouble/difficulty) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: conscience (sense of right and wrong — noun), conscientious (dutiful — adjective), conscious (aware). Do not confuse conscience/conscious.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: A myriad of possibilities unfolds when the artist embarks on the journey of creative experimentation.
option_2: A myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.
option_3: The myriad of possibilities unfolds when the artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.
option_4: The myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on the journey of creative experimentation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct usage is "a myriad of" (with the indefinite article "a"), and general statements use the indefinite article — "an artist", "a journey" — because no specific artist or journey is meant.

◦ Correct: A myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 3 and 4 wrongly use "The myriad" and specific "the" for general nouns.

• Option 1 uses "the artist" and "the journey", implying particular ones, which does not suit a general statement.

NOTE

• "Myriad" can be used as "a myriad of + plural noun" or simply "myriad + plural noun" (myriad possibilities). Use "a/an" for non-specific singular countable nouns in general statements.

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

The prisoners were living in appalling conditions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. shocking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Appalling" means causing horror or dismay; shockingly bad; dreadful. Its closest synonym is "shocking". (भयावह / अत्यंत बुरा)

◦ Example: The refugees were living in appalling/shocking conditions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "daring" (bold/courageous), Option 2 "ingenuous" (innocent/naive) and Option 3 "risky" (dangerous) do not match.

NOTE

• Synonyms of appalling: shocking, horrifying, dreadful, atrocious, terrible. Antonyms: pleasant, wonderful, admirable.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

One who brings a legal action against someone in court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Plaintiff.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "plaintiff" is a person who brings a case/legal action against another in a court of law. (वादी / मुद्दई)

◦ Example: The plaintiff filed a suit against the company for breach of contract.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sanctimonious" (making a show of being morally superior) is an adjective, not a person.

• Option 2 "Numismatic" relates to the study/collection of coins.

• Option 3 "Pragmatist" (a practical, realistic person) does not fit.

NOTE

• Legal one-word substitutes: plaintiff (one who sues), defendant (one who is sued), plaintiff vs. accused, witness (one who gives evidence), jury (a group deciding a verdict).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Absense.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Absense" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "absence" (with a "c"), meaning the state of being away/not present. (अनुपस्थिति)

◦ Spelling key: AB + SENCE → absence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Abstract" (not concrete), "Abscess" (a swollen area containing pus) and "Abstinent" (refraining from something) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related: absent (adjective), absence (noun), absentee (one who is absent). Note "absence" ends in "-ence", not "-ense".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

There have been numerous attempts made by the citizens to restore parity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Most numerous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the official answer key, the underlined segment "numerous" is to be substituted with the superlative form "most numerous", emphasising that the attempts made by the citizens were the greatest in number.

◦ Substituted: There have been most numerous attempts made by the citizens to restore parity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "More numerous" is a comparative and would need a "than" clause for a valid comparison.

• Option 4 "Quite numerous" merely softens the sense and was not the intended key.

NOTE

• Degrees of "numerous": numerous (positive) – more numerous (comparative, with "than") – most numerous (superlative). Always record the printed Correct Answer as the official key.

question:
Select the word that is opposite in meaning (ANTONYM) to the highlighted word in the given sentence.

We enjoyed the gentle breeze that was blowing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. violent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gentle" means mild, soft and calm. Its antonym is "violent", meaning forceful, fierce and intense. (कोमल का विलोम — प्रचंड / हिंसक)

◦ Example: The gentle breeze soon became a violent storm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "soft" is a synonym of gentle.

• Option 2 "garnished" (decorated) and Option 3 "modest" (humble) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gentle: mild, soft, tender, calm. Antonyms: violent, harsh, rough, fierce.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Siva is a hard worker. He works ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "hard" is an adverb meaning with great effort. Since Siva is a "hard worker", he "works hard". (कठिन परिश्रम से)

◦ Correct: Siva is a hard worker. He works hard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "hardly" is a different word meaning "scarcely / almost not", which would reverse the meaning (he hardly works = he barely works).

• Option 1 "bad" and Option 2 "scarcely" do not fit.

NOTE

• "Hard" and "hardly" are not related in meaning: "He works hard" (with effort) vs "He hardly works" (almost not at all). "Hard" is both an adjective and an adverb.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

I could _____ the reason for being _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. find; fined.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs a verb meaning "to discover" → "find". The second blank needs a word meaning "made to pay a penalty" → "fined". (कारण ढूँढ़ना; जुर्माना लगाया जाना)

◦ Correct: I could find the reason for being fined.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• These are homophones/near-homophones: find (discover) vs fined (penalised); bard (a poet) vs barred (blocked/prohibited).

• Options 1, 2 and 4 place these words where they make no sense.

NOTE

• Homophone sets to remember: find/fined, bard/barred, board/bored, plain/plane. Meaning decides the choice, not just sound.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Siliguri has joined the nation to celebrate the golden jubilee of the first conquest of Mount Everest by an Indian.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No improvement required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Siliguri has joined the nation to celebrate the golden jubilee ..." is already grammatically correct. The present perfect "has joined" + the infinitive of purpose "to celebrate" is proper.

◦ Correct (unchanged): Siliguri has joined the nation to celebrate the golden jubilee of the first conquest of Mount Everest by an Indian.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "joins the celebratory nation" changes the tense and meaning.

• Option 2 "joining the nation celebrate" is grammatically broken.

• Option 4 "joined the national celebration" alters the intended structure.

NOTE

• "To + verb" (infinitive of purpose) explains why an action is done: "joined ... to celebrate", "went ... to study". No change is needed when the original is already correct.

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
option_1: Our Principal is a great teacher and administrator.
option_2: Our Principal is a great teacher and a great administrator.
option_3: Our Principal is a great teacher and an administrator.
option_4: Our Principal is great teacher and administrator.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Our Principal is a great teacher and administrator.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When one person performs two roles, the article "a/an" is used only once before the first noun, and the adjective "great" applies to both: "a great teacher and administrator" (one and the same person).

◦ Correct: Our Principal is a great teacher and administrator.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "a great teacher and a great administrator" would suggest they may be two different persons (article repeated).

• Option 3 mixes articles incorrectly; Option 4 omits the necessary article "a".

NOTE

• Rule: one article for one person/thing in two capacities (a poet and philosopher = same person); repeat the article for two separate persons/things (a poet and a philosopher = two people).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence.

If the two families could forget their past quarrels forever, both could benefit immensely.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. bury the hatchet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "bury the hatchet" means to end a quarrel and make peace; to forget past disputes. It fits "forget their past quarrels forever". (पुराना झगड़ा भुलाकर सुलह कर लेना)

◦ Correct: If the two families could bury the hatchet, both could benefit immensely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "cut to the quick" = to hurt someone's feelings deeply.

• Option 2 "catch a tartar" = to deal with someone more powerful than expected.

• Option 3 "do a good turn" = to do a kind/helpful act.

NOTE

• Similar peace idioms: "bury the hatchet", "make up", "let bygones be bygones", "mend fences".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Presumably
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Unlikely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Presumably" means very probably; as may reasonably be assumed/likely. Its antonym is "unlikely" (not probable). (संभवतः का विलोम — असंभावित)

◦ Example: He will presumably (likely) come — as opposed to it being unlikely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Certainly" (definitely) is closer to a synonym in the sense of assurance.

• Options 2 "Liberally" and 4 "Successfully" are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of presumably: probably, likely, seemingly, apparently. Antonyms: unlikely, improbably, doubtfully.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. satisfaction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage praises reading as beneficial, so "one gets mental satisfaction" (a feeling of contentment/fulfilment) fits the positive tone. (मानसिक संतुष्टि)

◦ Correct: As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental satisfaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "coverage" and Option 2 "success" do not collocate naturally with "mental" here.

• Option 4 "exhaustion" (tiredness) has a negative sense that contradicts the passage.

NOTE

• Collocations with "mental": mental satisfaction, mental peace, mental strength, mental health. Choose the word that matches the overall positive tone of the passage.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. knowledge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reading "helps us acquire knowledge" — information, facts and understanding — which links naturally to the next idea of intellectual growth. (ज्ञान अर्जित करना)

◦ Correct: It helps us acquire knowledge and attain intellectual expansion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "readiness", Option 2 "employment" and Option 4 "strategies" do not fit the idea of what reading primarily gives us.

• "Acquire knowledge" is a very common and natural collocation.

NOTE

• Common collocations: acquire knowledge, gain experience, develop skills. The intellectual theme of the passage points to "knowledge".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. expansion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reading helps us "attain intellectual expansion" — a broadening/growth of the mind and understanding. This matches the theme of intellectual benefit. (बौद्धिक विस्तार)

◦ Correct: It helps us acquire knowledge and attain intellectual expansion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "stagnation" (no growth) and Option 3 "compression" (reduction) are the opposite of growth.

• Option 1 "creation" does not collocate well with "intellectual".

NOTE

• "Intellectual expansion/growth/development" all convey the broadening of the mind. Pick the positive, growth-oriented word to match the passage.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. boredom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reading takes away our boredom" — it removes dullness and keeps the mind engaged. This is a well-known benefit of reading. (ऊब / नीरसता दूर करना)

◦ Correct: Reading takes away our boredom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "vigour" (energy) is positive — reading would not "take away" something good.

• Options 1 "time" and 4 "concern" do not fit as well as "boredom" in this positive context.

NOTE

• "Take away boredom" means to relieve/remove dullness. Choose the negative feeling that reading is said to remove.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________ and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. comfort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reading "can bring comfort in our sorrowful times" — it provides solace and consolation when we are sad. This matches the emotional benefit mentioned earlier. (सांत्वना / आराम)

◦ Correct: Reading can bring comfort in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "resentment" (bitterness), Option 3 "lethargy" (laziness) and Option 4 "oppression" (cruel treatment) all carry negative meanings that clash with "sorrowful times".

NOTE

• Synonyms of comfort: solace, consolation, relief, reassurance. In sad times we seek comfort, not resentment or oppression.
